div.div: زِقٌّ [A skin for holding wine &c.:] any receptacle, consisting of a skin, that is used for wine and the like: or, as some say, not thus called unless it be stripped off from the part next the animal's neck: or, accord. to AHn, one in which wine is conveyed: (M:) or a skin for water or milk; syn. سِقَآءٌ: (S, K:) or a skin of which the hair is clipped, not plucked out, (Lth, K,) for wine and the like, (Lth,) or for wine &c.: (K:) or a receptacle, (ظَرْفٌ, Msb, and Har p. 335,) of skin, in which are put clarified butter and vinegar and wine: (Har ibid.:) or, as some say, a ظَرْف smeared with زِفْت: (Msb:) AHát says that it is such as is smeared with زِفْت or with قِير: (TA:) pl. (of pauc., S) أَزْقَاقٌ (S, M, Msb, K) and أَزُقٌّ, mentioned by El-Hejeree, (M,) and (of mult., S) زِقَاقٌ (S, M, K) and زُقَّانٌ [in the CK erroneously written رُقّاقٌ]. (S, M, Msb, K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
